answer: Mass identity fraud is unattractive here not because it is always caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale — the expected loss from slashing and rejection exceeds the expected gain. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a vine as the anchor of the cost.
